name: Ethereum
summary: Ethereum is the primary settlement environment for DeFi, tokenized assets, stablecoins, staking, governance, and on-chain financial infrastructure.
environment: Ethereum systems often concentrate high value in upgradeable contracts, privileged roles, vault accounting, oracle dependencies, governance paths, and integrations with established DeFi liquidity.

name: Arbitrum
summary: Arbitrum is a major Ethereum rollup used by DeFi protocols, derivatives markets, lending systems, and asset infrastructure.
environment: Arbitrum projects inherit EVM smart contract risk while adding bridge, sequencer, retryable ticket, cross-domain message, liquidity, and L2 operational assumptions.

name: Base
summary: Base provides Ethereum scaling for consumer finance, payments, DeFi applications, and institutional on-chain products.
environment: Base reviews combine EVM contract security with L2 bridge assumptions, OP Stack behavior, account abstraction patterns, and production controls around high-volume user flows.

name: Optimism
summary: Optimism and OP Mainnet support cost-efficient DeFi, governance, payment, and appchain-adjacent ecosystems across the Superchain.
environment: Optimism security work covers EVM logic, OP Stack deployment behavior, cross-domain messaging, withdrawal mechanics, governance controls, and Superchain integrations.

name: Polygon
summary: Polygon supports DeFi, tokenized assets, gaming, payments, enterprise blockchain deployments, and high-volume EVM applications.
environment: Polygon reviews focus on EVM contract behavior, bridge assumptions, validator and finality considerations, oracle integrations, high-volume token flows, and upgrade safety.

name: Avalanche
summary: Avalanche supports DeFi, app-specific networks, institutional deployments, tokenized assets, and high-throughput EVM applications.
environment: Avalanche security reviews include C-Chain EVM contracts, subnet architecture, bridge assumptions, staking and validator concerns, oracle integrations, and custom financial application logic.

name: BNB Smart Chain
summary: BNB Smart Chain supports high-volume DeFi, exchanges, token launches, payment flows, and retail-facing EVM applications.
environment: BNB Smart Chain reviews focus on EVM contract risk, privileged controls, token mechanics, liquidity dependencies, bridge integrations, and transaction-ordering assumptions in fast-moving markets.

name: Scroll
summary: Scroll is a zkEVM scaling environment for Ethereum applications that need EVM compatibility with zero-knowledge rollup architecture.
environment: Scroll security reviews combine normal EVM contract analysis with rollup bridge assumptions, prover and finality considerations, cross-chain state movement, and zkEVM-specific deployment behavior.

name: Linea
summary: Linea is an EVM-compatible zero-knowledge rollup used for scalable Ethereum applications, DeFi, payments, and on-chain products.
environment: Linea reviews cover EVM contract logic, zkEVM deployment assumptions, canonical bridge dependencies, finality expectations, and integration risk across Ethereum and L2 liquidity.

name: ZKsync
language: Solidity, EraVM, and account abstraction patterns
summary: ZKsync supports scalable Ethereum applications with native account abstraction, zk rollup settlement, and evolving developer tooling.
environment: ZKsync reviews account for EVM-like code, EraVM differences, account abstraction behavior, paymaster logic, bridge flows, and contract deployment patterns that differ from Ethereum mainnet.

name: Solana
language: Rust, Anchor, and native Solana programs
summary: Solana supports high-throughput financial applications, exchanges, payments, token programs, and consumer-scale on-chain systems.
environment: Solana security reviews focus on account validation, signer authority, PDA derivation, CPI boundaries, Anchor constraints, rent and lamport handling, and assumptions created by parallel execution.

name: Aptos
language: Move modules and Aptos transaction logic
summary: Aptos supports Move-based applications, asset systems, DeFi protocols, payment flows, and high-throughput on-chain financial products.
environment: Aptos reviews focus on Move resource semantics, object ownership, signer authority, module upgrade patterns, token standards, transaction scripts, and financial invariants around asset movement.

name: Sui
language: Sui Move modules and object-centric transaction logic
summary: Sui supports object-centric Move applications, DeFi protocols, gaming economies, token systems, and high-throughput consumer finance products.
environment: Sui security reviews cover object ownership, shared object concurrency, capability patterns, package upgrades, programmable transaction blocks, token standards, and financial logic built around Sui Move.

name: Canton
language: Daml smart contracts and Canton application logic
summary: Canton supports institutional digital asset workflows, privacy-preserving settlement, tokenized assets, and regulated financial market infrastructure.
environment: Canton reviews focus on Daml contract logic, participant permissions, privacy boundaries, settlement workflows, authorization rules, interoperability assumptions, and operational controls around institutional deployments.

name: Starknet
summary: Starknet supports Cairo-native applications, account abstraction, DeFi protocols, application-specific logic, and validity-rollup infrastructure.
environment: Starknet security reviews focus on Cairo contract behavior, account abstraction, component composition, storage layout, L1/L2 messaging, bridge assumptions, and proof-system-driven execution expectations.
